Recreation & Community Services Commission
MINUTES
CITY OF BALDWIN PARK
Recreation & Community Services Commission
MONDAY, APRIL 07, 2014
5:00 p.m. COUNCIL CHAMBERS
14403 E. Pacific Avenue
Baldwin Park
Leslie Brito, Arcelia Avila, Ana Lujan, JoAnn Watkins, Commissioners
&nbsp
Vacant, Vacant, Student Commissioner
The Recreation & Community Services Commission of the City of Baldwin Park met in REGULAR SESSION at the above time and place.
CALL TO ORDER
ROLL CALL
Present: Irma Tarango, Kimberly Liau, Alfredo Orozco, Martha Reyes, Ruth Viveros, Jo Ann Watkins.
Absent: Cecelia D. Bernal.
Also Present: Manuel Carrillo, Jr., Director of Recreation & Community Services, Armando Nava, Program Coordinator, Vanessa Carbajal, Program Coordinator, Cindy Lopez, Auqatics Manager, Teresa Alexander, City Service Worker.
APPROVAL OF CERTIFICATE OF POSTING FOR MAY 5, 2014.
Montion was made to approve the Certificate of Posting for May 5, 2014. M/S/C: WATKINS/ OROZCO.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF APRIL 7, 2014.
Montion was made to approve the Minutes for April 7, 2014. M/S/C: OROZCO/WATKINS.
PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS
None.
REPORTS OF OFFICERS, COMMISSIONERS, OR COMMITTEES.
1. Community Development Block Grant Update
Director Manuel Carrillo Jr. gave the Commissioners an update regarding the California Development Block Grant. Council has approved the following amounts for the 2014 - 2015 Fiscal Year; Child Care Subsidy was not funded this year. The Department requested $2,100 and the joint Commission recommended $0 and the Council agreed with the Commission. The Family Service Center was funded, the Department requested $30,000 and the joint Commission agreed and the Council approved $28,500. The Recreation Sports Scholarship was funded, the Department requested $15,000 and the joint Commission agreed and the Council approved $12,350. The Youth Employment was funded, the Department requested $24,000 and the joint Commission recommended $21,149 and the Council approved $14,449. Manuel Carrillo Jr. was very happy to see that the Youth Employment was able to receive more funding then last year and with the Youth Employment staff we will be able to supplement our year round staff. In the past we have also been able to hire some of our Youth Employment staff as our Recreation Leaders.
2. Recreational Scholarship Program Update
Program Coordinator, Armando Nava , gave the Commissioners an update regarding the Recreation al Scholarship Program. He asked the Commissioners if they still wanted to continue with the date, Friday, July 25 th for the Texas Holdâ€™em Tournament Fundraiser. The Commissioners agreed and Armando Nava informed the Commission that the fundraiser will be promoted at the Summer Concerts. He also shared with the Commissioners that Cindy Lopez, Aquatics manager and Lifeguards hosted a Texas Holdâ€™em Tournament a few weeks ago for the Baldwin Park Piranha Swim Team and had a really good turn out. He is hoping that with the new players that attended the Swim team fundraiser the will also want to attend the Recreation al Scholarship Fundraiser. Armando Nava informed the Commissioners that there is currently $2,000 in the scholarship account and he is hoping to build that amount up for the students. Director Manuel Carrillo Jr. encouraged the Commissioners to attend and bring family and friends to participate. The more people that participate the more money we will be able to distribute to the scholarship recipients. He also shared with the Commission that if there is anyone who doesnâ€™t know how to play Texas Holdâ€™em, there will be someone teaching them how to play at the beginning of the night. There is plenty of food as well as adult beverages and raffles for the night. Manuel Carrillo Jr. is hoping that by promoting it at the Summer Concert on Thursday, July 24 th they will get more people to attend the fundraiser on Friday, July 25 th at the Julia McNeil Senior Center . Program Coordinator, Armando Nava also informed the Commission that the applications to apply for the scholarship are available on the City of Baldwin Park â€™s website, the front counter of the Esther Snyder Community Center , at the Terri Muse Family Service Center and at the High School in the career centers. The deadline to turn in the applications is Thursday, May 1 st . The following week Armando Nava will review the applications and then he will be setting up interviews with the commissioners the week of May 12 th . Director Manuel Carrillo Jr. informed the Commission that the department will recognize the winners at the Thursday, July 10 th summer concert. Armando Nava also asked the Commissioners to please help out with the raffle prizes. He will also see if he can get some autographed photos of a Pro golfer Lizette Salas. Commissioner Orozco asked if there were soccer teams for children/teens with disabilityâ€™s. Armando Nava informed Commissioner Orozco that we have an age limit for the sports department. Our age limit for sports is 8 th grade. Director Manuel Carrillo Jr. informed the Commissioners that we have a application that they can fill out and apply to use the field for their own teams, but we do not have anything for the older kids in High School.
3. Arbor Day Update
Program Coordinator, Vanessa Carbajal gave the Commissioners an update regarding the Arbor Day event. Vanessa Carbajal handed out a rough draft of the Arbor Day flyer that had just been approved. The final printed copies will be available on Wednesday and will be distributed to the schools on Friday. The Arbor Day event will take place on April 26 th at 10am until 1pm . The event will take place in the open grass area in front of the Esther Snyder Community Center . The vendors that will be participating are Waste Management, CCPHA/BPRAC, Upper San Gabriel Valley Water District, Home Depot, Valley County , and Public Works. The sponsors that have helped make this event possible are Waste Management, Allan Co. and Upper SGV Water District. The Arbor Day event will include FREE Mulch giveaway available from 9am to 2pm and the limit is 2 50lbs bags. If there is still mulch at 2:00pm and residents are stilling coming, they will still be able to get some. There will also be free food for the first 200 guests that complete a passport pass. The first 250 guest will be eligible to receive a used motor oil recycled container. Vanessa Carbajal also informed the commissioners that there will be crafts and a bouncy house for the kids. This year there will be a FAMILY ART SCULPTURE CONTEST that will take place the day of the event. The subject is SCULPTURE and it has to be made of nature (plant life/trees) and recyclable material. The sculpture will be judged on creativity and craftsmanship. The artwork will need to be submitted between 10am and 11am and the winners will be announced at 12:30pm on Saturday, April 26 th . Manuel Carrillo Jr. asked the Commissioners to please put it in their calendars to attend. Manuel Carrillo Jr. asked to have the Summer Lunch update pushed back to the May Commission meeting.
4. Summer Lunch Update
Manuel Carrillo Jr., Director of Recreation & Community Services asked if this item could be pushed back to the May 7, 2014 Recreation Commission Meeting.
5. Program Specialist Introduction
Director Manuel Carrillo Jr. introduced Cindy Lopez, Aquatics Manager. He informed the commissioners that his goal is to introduce the key staff to the Commission and familiarize them with each other. Aquatics Manager/ Program Specialist are key part-time staff members within the Recreation Department. Manuel Carrillo Jr. read a short bio about Cindy Lopez; she started with the Recreation Department May 2007 as a seasonal Lifeguard. In 2008, she was certified as a Water Safety Instructor (WSI) and began teaching swim lessons. In 2010, Cindy Lopez started coaching the Baldwin Park Piranha Swim Team until 2013. In May 2013, Cindy Lopez obtained her current position as Aquatics Manager and over sees the entire Aquatics Division. In the busy months of summer, Cindy Lopez oversees 30-40 lifeguards, WSI, coaches, cashiers. Manuel Carrillo Jr. informed the Commissioners that since Cindy Lopez is located in the administration office, she is also assigned to special projects throughout the year. Cindy Lopez grew up in the City of Baldwin Park and currently resides in the City of Glendora and also works for the City of Los Angeles in their Parks Department. Cindy Lopez was able to attend the California Parks and Recreation Society Conference in Ontario this year where she was able to network with other Parks and Recreation professionals. Cindy Lopez is a young professional making her way through the Recreation and Community Services field. The Recreation Commissioners welcomed Aquatics Manager, Cindy Lopez.
6. Commissioners Application Update
Teresa Alexander, City Service Worker gave the Commissioners an update regarding the Recreation Commission applications. All applications are due to the City Clerks office by May 1 st . The City Clerks office will stamp them when they receive it and then it will be sent over to the Recreation Department. If you have a question regarding your application, you can call the City Clerks office or Teresa Alexander. Director, Manuel Carrillo Jr. thanked Teresa Alexander for all of her hard work with the department.
COMMISSION REQUESTS AND COMMUNICATIONS
Director, Manuel Carrillo Jr. gave the Commissioners an update regarding the CPRS ( California Parks and Recreation Society) District 13 awards. The department received an award for the Senior Center 20 th Prom as well as the MAPS for College. Manuel Carrillo Jr. also wanted to congratulate the District 13 th newly installed Vice President, Vanessa Carbajal. Next year she will continue to grow and will be Madame President of District 13 CPRS. This will mark our second President to come from Baldwin Park , with Helen Hernandez being past president. Manuel Carrillo Jr also wanted to congratulate Vanessa Carbajal on graduating from La Verne University with her Master in Public Administration. Commissioners congratulated Vanessa Carbajal on her accomplishments.
ADJOURNMENT
With no other business being presented, Chairperson Tarango adjourned the meeting at 5:25pm. M/S/C: WATKINS/ REYES.
